argument_summary: Certification remains supportable on the admissible record only as a caveated certification theory. The record supports deployment readiness in the aggregate because the release cleared launch readiness by 2.3 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance supports managing residual AI risk through measurement and monitoring in deployment. The same record also shows that Spanish-language billing-ticket triage remains below target, the runbook is still a draft with owner and acceptance threshold TBD, and policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. The narrow, supportable position is therefore: certify, but only with the Spanish billing issue explicitly disclosed as a material limitation and with the draft runbook described as mitigation-in-progress rather than completed approval.
claims_about_business_cost: Unnecessary escalation would add launch friction even though the aggregate release signal is positive, but that cost does not justify overstating the state of mitigation. The lower-cost path consistent with the admissible record is to avoid escalation beyond a bounded caveat: certify with corrected disclosure and treat monitoring and rollback as ongoing controls rather than proof of closure.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not support clean certification without caveats on this record. Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents support readiness, but they do not eliminate the disclosure predicate for a current material weakness in a named launch use case. The draft runbook does not satisfy the policy standard for an approved mitigation because the required governance elements are incomplete. The compliant reading is caveated certification conditioned on accurate disclosure, not no-caveat certification and not treating the draft mitigation as closure.
concessions: The current record does not support certification without material caveats.
The draft runbook is not an approved mitigation under the stated policy because owner and acceptance threshold remain TBD.
The model-card draft language stating there are no known material limitations is inconsistent with the unresolved Spanish-language billing issue and should not be relied on as-is.
No new evidence is available to show that disclosure has already been corrected or that formal risk acceptance has been approved.
